commits.author: Boris
commits.subject: fix(cron): persist last_fire_attempted_at to prevent crash-mid-fire double-fire
commits.body:
Iter 11 fix for the iter 10 audit: if the daemon crashed between
sc.firing=true and the post-success updateCron persist, nothing on disk
recorded the attempt. On restart, loadCrons computed referenceMs from
the stale last_fired_at and the catch-up gate fired the same logical
slot a second time — guaranteed double-fire on every crash mid-fire.

The scheduler now writes last_fire_attempted_at = now to crons.json
BEFORE awaiting onFire, and loadCrons includes it in the referenceMs
candidates. Crash mid-fire → restart sees attempted_at = T → reference
is current → nextFireAt is in the future → no catch-up.

Tradeoff: a fire whose dispatch genuinely failed before the current
process crashed will be skipped one window. Acceptable, because the
alternative (guaranteed double-fire on every crash) is worse — and the
existing dispatch-failed branch already advances nextFireAt for the
same reason.

Three integration tests in phase5 were asserting the old "catch-up
after a failed-fire window" behavior, which iter 11 intentionally
suppresses. They now advance to the next scheduled slot to verify
normal forward scheduling resumes after recovery.

Iter 10 audit test flipped from asserting 2 fires (the bug) to
asserting 1 fire (the fix); inline it.todo placeholder removed.

Tests: 1436 passing | 1 skipped | 0 failing.

commits.author: Boris
commits.subject: test(cron): pin iter 12 — concurrent bus update-cron lost-update race
commits.body:
8 parallel `node dist/cli.js bus update-cron` child processes against
the same agent (each updating a distinct cron name) reliably lose
multiple mutations: 15/40 updates lost across 5 iterations in the
repro.  Root cause: addCron / updateCron / removeCron all do
`readCrons -> mutate -> writeCrons` with no inter-process lock, so
two writers that interleave between read and write overwrite each
other.  atomicWriteSync (tmp + rename) is per-write only — it does
NOT make the read-modify-write sequence transactional.

Test pins the bug.  Iter 12 fix will add a proper-lockfile-style
file lock around the read-modify-write sequence in src/bus/crons.ts
and flip this test from failing to passing.

commits.author: Boris
commits.subject: fix(cron): serialize bus add/remove/update-cron to fix iter 12 lost-update race
commits.body:
Wraps the read-modify-write block in addCron/removeCron/updateCron with
withFileLockSync (utils/lock.ts), a new helper that retries acquireLock
with exponential backoff up to 5s.

Pre-fix the integration test (concurrent-cron-mutations) lost 15/40
mutations across 5 iterations because two CLI processes could readCrons
while a third was mid-write. The rename in atomicWriteSync only made
each individual write atomic, not the surrounding transaction.

Also tightens acquireLock:
- Treat only EEXIST as contention; propagate other fs errors (EACCES,
  ENOSPC, EROFS) so a read-only or full filesystem surfaces the actual
  cause instead of looping until timeout.
- When EEXIST + missing PID file, refuse rather than steal. A missing
  PID file just means the holder is between mkdir and writeFileSync;
  the right move is to refuse and let the caller retry. Pre-fix that
  gap let two acquirers BOTH believe they held the lock, the actual
  mechanism behind the iter 12 race.

withFileLockSync uses process.hrtime.bigint() for timeout tracking so
it terminates correctly even under vi.useFakeTimers() (where Date.now
is frozen). Without this, phase5-failure-modes hung indefinitely when
chmod 0o555 caused an EACCES fall through the retry loop.

Closes iter 12.

commits.author: Boris
commits.subject: feat(cli): add bus upgrade-cron-teaching scanner (Part A of #292 follow-up)
commits.body:
Adds 'cortextos bus upgrade-cron-teaching [agent]' to scan an agent's
workspace for stale CronCreate / /loop / config.json cron-registration
teaching that pre-dates the external-persistent-crons migration.

Scope per agent: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, ONBOARDING.md, and
.claude/skills/**/SKILL.md.

Detection patterns (per-line):
- \\bCronCreate\\b
- /loop create cron
- /loop <interval> in cron-registration form
- (configured in config.json)
- edit/modify config.json combined with cron context

Whitelist (lines NOT flagged):
- Lines containing negation tokens: 'do NOT', 'Never use',
  'session-only', 'evaporate', 'recurring: false', etc. These are
  teaching the deprecation, not recommending the stale path.
- Files containing the m2c1-worker sentinel comment
  ('/loop is intentionally used') are skipped wholesale. The worker
  /loop is a legitimate short-lived session-scoped poll.

Default mode is scan-only. --apply performs only the safe literal
substitutions known not to depend on surrounding context. The only
substitution today is '(configured in config.json)' to '(configured
via cortextos bus add-cron)', the same precedent set in dc9e296e.
CronCreate / /loop matches are reported but never mechanically
rewritten because the surrounding sentence usually needs human edits.

CLI behavior:
- 'bus upgrade-cron-teaching <agent>': scan one agent, exit 1 if any
  stale ref found.
- 'bus upgrade-cron-teaching' (no arg): scan every agent under
  orgs/*/agents/.
- --json: machine-readable output.
- --apply: in-place safe substitutions.

Tests: 18 unit tests cover pattern detection, sentinel handling,
negation context, and apply-mode safety. 6 integration tests drive
the compiled dist/cli.js against tmp fixtures and verify --json /
--apply / agent resolution / all-agents form.

Part A of three: Part B updates CRONS_MIGRATION_GUIDE.md, Part C
adds a daemon first-boot advisory banner that runs the same scanner.

commits.subject: docs(migration): document upgrade-cron-teaching for existing workspaces (Part B)
commits.body:
Adds a new "Upgrading Existing Agent Skill/Bootstrap Files" section to
CRONS_MIGRATION_GUIDE.md after "Manual Migration". The auto-migration
handles cron data only; pre-migration agent workspaces still teach the
deprecated CronCreate / /loop / config.json patterns. This section
explains what the cortextos bus upgrade-cron-teaching scanner detects,
the canonical replacement teaching (with one-line examples), the --apply
and --json flags, and the whitelist mechanics (per-line negation tokens
and the m2c1-worker /loop is intentionally used sentinel).

Cites the canonical anchors at templates/agent/CLAUDE.md:27,120 and
templates/agent/AGENTS.md:33,419, plus the three template-sweep commits
(70d11dab, a47b1e4d, dc9e296e).

Adds tests/integration/migration-guide-references-upgrade-cmd.test.ts as
a regression guard so we don't lose the reference: asserts the heading,
the cortextos bus upgrade-cron-teaching command string, both flags, the
whitelist mechanics, and that the section is positioned between Manual
Migration and Troubleshooting.

Full suite: 1467 passed, 1 skipped (was 1461 + 1 skipped before this
change; +6 tests = the new file). Typecheck clean.

+## Upgrading Existing Agent Skill/Bootstrap Files
+
+The auto-migration handles cron *data* (`config.json` -> `crons.json`). It does not touch the cron *teaching* in your agent's bootstrap, skill, and onboarding files. Pre-migration workspaces frequently still tell the agent to use `CronCreate`, `/loop`, or hand-edit `config.json` to register a cron. After the switch to external persistent crons, every one of those instructions is wrong: `CronCreate` and `/loop` are session-only and evaporate on restart, and `config.json` is no longer the cron source of truth (the daemon owns `crons.json` directly).
+
+The repo-shipped templates were swept clean in `0ccb3c98`, `b10711a4`, and `836f4759`. End-user agent workspaces created before that sweep need their own pass. The `cortextos bus upgrade-cron-teaching` command exists to find and (where safe) fix those leftovers.
+
+### What Gets Detected
+
+The scanner walks `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `ONBOARDING.md`, and every `.claude/skills/**/SKILL.md` under the agent dir. It flags any line matching one of these patterns:
+
+| Pattern | What it catches | Why it's wrong |
+|---|---|---|
+| `\bCronCreate\b` | Bare references to the `CronCreate` tool | `CronCreate` is for one-shot in-session reminders only. Persistent crons must use `cortextos bus add-cron`. |
+| `/loop create cron` | The legacy "create cron via /loop" form | `/loop` is session-only and dies on restart. |
+| `/loop <interval>` (e.g. `/loop 4h`, `/loop 30m`) | The "/loop your-prompt" cron-registration form | Same: session-only. |
+| `(configured in config.json)` | Stale parenthetical about cron source-of-truth | Cron source of truth is now `crons.json`, written by `cortextos bus add-cron`. |
+| `edit config.json` paired with `cron` on the same line | Operator instructions to hand-edit cron entries | The daemon owns `crons.json`. Hand-editing `config.json` no longer registers a cron. |
+
+The canonical replacement teaching lives at:
+
+- `templates/agent/CLAUDE.md` line 27 (session-start cron note) and line 120 (Crons section)
+- `templates/agent/AGENTS.md` line 33 (session-start cron note) and line 419 (runtime add-cron instruction)
+
+One-line replacement examples:
+
+| Old | New |
+|---|---|
+| `Use CronCreate to schedule a 4h heartbeat` | `cortextos bus add-cron $CTX_AGENT_NAME heartbeat 4h '<prompt>'` |
+| `/loop 4h heartbeat` | `cortextos bus add-cron $CTX_AGENT_NAME heartbeat 4h heartbeat` |
+| `/loop create cron name=heartbeat ...` | `cortextos bus add-cron <agent> <name> <interval> <prompt>` |
+| `(configured in config.json)` | `(configured via cortextos bus add-cron)` |
+| `Edit config.json to add the cron entry` | `Run cortextos bus add-cron <agent> <name> <interval> <prompt>` |
+
+### Running the Scanner
+
+```bash
+# Scan one agent (exits 1 if any matches remain)
+cortextos bus upgrade-cron-teaching <agent>
+
+# Scan every enabled agent under orgs/*/agents/*
+cortextos bus upgrade-cron-teaching
+
+# Machine-readable output for scripting / CI
+cortextos bus upgrade-cron-teaching <agent> --json
+
+# Apply the safe literal substitutions in-place
+cortextos bus upgrade-cron-teaching <agent> --apply
+```
+
+The non-zero exit on any match makes this safe to wire into a pre-commit hook or CI gate.
+
+### Whitelist Mechanics
+
+Two opt-outs prevent false positives on lines that intentionally talk about the old patterns:
+
+- **Per-line negation tokens.** If a line contains `do NOT`, `Never use`, `won't survive`, `session-only`, `evaporate`, `recurring: false`, or `deprecated`, the scanner skips it. This covers teaching-by-deprecation prose like *"Do NOT use CronCreate for persistent scheduling."*
+- **Per-file sentinel marker.** A file containing the literal string `/loop is intentionally used` is skipped wholesale. This is the m2c1-worker carve-out: m2c1 worker agents legitimately use short-lived `/loop` for in-session task queueing, not for persistent crons.
+
+### What `--apply` Will and Won't Touch
+
+`--apply` performs only the safe literal substitution `(configured in config.json)` -> `(configured via cortextos bus add-cron)`. Everything else is reported but not rewritten. `CronCreate` and `/loop` matches in particular need a manual edit, because the surrounding sentence almost always has to change with them: a sentence like *"Use CronCreate to schedule X"* cannot be mechanically repaired without rewriting the verb and operand. Read the scanner report, then edit by hand using the canonical replacements above.
+
+---
+
 ## Troubleshooting
 
 **Cron not firing:**

+    expect(manualIdx).toBeGreaterThan(-1);
+    expect(upgradeIdx).toBeGreaterThan(manualIdx);
+    expect(troubleshootIdx).toBeGreaterThan(upgradeIdx);

commits.subject: feat(daemon): emit cron-teaching upgrade banner during migrate-crons (Part C)
commits.body:
Wires the cron-teaching scanner into the per-agent migration path so the
daemon advises operators when an agent workspace still contains stale
CronCreate / /loop / config.json teaching after the cron-data migration
has run.

Behavior:
  - migrateCronsForAgent now invokes runTeachingCheck after the data
    migration completes, on every status (migrated, no-config, no-crons,
    skipped-already-migrated). Pure advisory: a non-fatal scan failure
    is caught and logged, never blocks the migration result.
  - One log line per agent on stale matches:
      [<agent>] cron-teaching upgrade recommended: N stale references
      in K files. Run cortextos bus upgrade-cron-teaching <agent>
  - Drops a .cron-teaching-checked marker (next to .crons-migrated in
    the agent state dir) so subsequent boots do not re-warn. Marker is
    written even when matches=0, so clean workspaces are also single-
    shot.
  - Honors options.force: deletes the .cron-teaching-checked marker so
    the scan re-runs alongside the existing crons-migrated re-run.

Implementation:
  - Existing migrateCronsForAgent body extracted into private
    runMigrationCore(); the public entry point is now a thin wrapper
    that runs the migration, then runTeachingCheck, then returns.
  - New helpers: teachingMarkerPath, isTeachingChecked (exported for
    tests), writeTeachingMarker, deleteTeachingMarker, runTeachingCheck.
  - Reuses scanAgentDir from src/utils/cron-teaching-scanner.ts so the
    detection patterns and whitelist mechanics (negation tokens +
    sentinel marker) stay in lockstep with the CLI command.

Tests:
  - tests/integration/cron-migration-banner.test.ts (7 cases):
      1. Banner fires with stale references and includes
         [<agent>], the run command, and the count phrasing.
      2. Banner suppressed on second run after marker is dropped.
      3. force: true re-runs the scan.
      4. Marker still dropped when no stale references exist.
      5. Sentinel marker (/loop is intentionally used) suppresses the
         file from the scan, so a worker-style file does not trigger
         a banner.
      6. Workspace dir gone -> migration returns no-config, marker is
         still dropped, no banner is emitted.
      7. Corrupt config.json still allows the advisory to run against
         the surrounding workspace files.

Full suite: 1474 passed, 1 skipped (was 1467 + 1 skipped; +7 new tests).
Typecheck clean. dist rebuilt; CLI integration tests still green.

Part A: eb3ddf3c (scanner + bus upgrade-cron-teaching CLI).
Part B: 49e57558 (CRONS_MIGRATION_GUIDE.md section + regression test).
Part C: this commit. Three-part series complete; James's merge call still
gates feat/external-persistent-crons.

commits.subject: fix(daemon): drop redundant agent-name prefix from cron-teaching banner
commits.body:
The per-agent logger already prefixes lines with `[<agent>] [migration] `,
so the inner `[<agent>] ` literal in runTeachingCheck and the failure
catch-path produced doubled prefixes in the live log:

    [boris] [migration] [boris] cron-teaching upgrade recommended: ...

After this change the message is identifier-free and the daemon's
existing per-agent logger supplies the single prefix:

    [boris] [migration] cron-teaching upgrade recommended: ...

The agent name is still present at the end of the banner inside the
`Run cortextos bus upgrade-cron-teaching <agent>` suggestion.

Test updates: the unit test exercises migrateCronsForAgent with a plain
log function (no daemon prefix wrapper), so the prior `expect(banner).
toContain('[banner-test]')` was leaning on the redundant prefix. Replaced
with an explicit assertion that the banner starts with
`cron-teaching upgrade recommended` to lock the new shape in.

-- `updateCron` not called (no fire_count increment on failure).
-
-**Test 4c — Retry timing validation:**
-- Measured `Date.now()` at each call via fake timers.
-- Gap 1 (after attempt 1): 1000ms (matches 1s backoff).
-- Gap 2 (after attempt 2): 4000ms (matches 4s backoff).
-- Gap 3 (after attempt 3): 16000ms (matches 16s backoff).
-- Timing matched within ±1000ms tolerance (fake timer precision).
-
-**Retry backoff schedule**: 1s → 4s → 16s. Total max retry window: 21 seconds.
-
-### Scenario 5: Concurrent cron fires
-
-**Status**: PASSED (2 test cases) | **Wall time**: 5ms / 3ms
-
-**Test 5a — 5 interval crons (catch-up fire):**
-- All 5 crons had `last_fired_at` 25h ago; all had `nextFireAt = now` on scheduler start.
-- All 5 fired sequentially within the first tick.
-- All 5 log entries present with `status=fired`.
-- `crons.json` atomic writes: all 5 `last_fired_at` fields updated, all `fire_count=1`.
-- No lost updates — atomic write via `atomicWriteSync` (temp-file + rename) prevents torn writes.
-
-**Test 5b — 3 cron-expression crons (same schedule):**
-- All 3 used `*/5 * * * *`; all fired at same tick boundary.
-- All 3 present in log after one scheduling window (5 min + one tick).
-
-**Race conditions**: None observed. Sequential iteration in `tick()` combined with atomic disk writes prevents state corruption even when multiple crons fire in the same tick.
-
-### Scenario 6: Log integrity end-to-end
-
-**Status**: PASSED | **Wall time**: 165ms (24h simulation)
-
-- 3 agents, 6 crons, 24h simulation.
-- Post-simulation integrity checks:
-  - No orphaned log entries (entries for non-existent crons).
-  - No cross-agent log contamination (entries only appear in their owning agent's log).
-  - No missing entries: `fired` log count == actual observed fire count for every cron.
-  - Total `fired` entries across all agents == sum of `fireCounts` map.
-  - All `fired` entries have `error=null`.
-  - All `retried`/`failed` entries have non-null `error`.
-  - All entries have required fields: `ts`, `cron`, `attempt >= 1`, `duration_ms >= 0`.
-
-**Log completeness**: 100% across all agents and cron schedules.

-
-| Metric | Value |

-| Scenarios passing | 6/6 |

-| Atomic write race conditions observed | 0 |

-| Regressions in existing 797 tests | 0 |

-
-## Architecture Notes
-
-**Timer strategy**: `vi.useFakeTimers()` intercepts the scheduler's `setInterval` (30s tick) and `fireWithRetry`'s `setTimeout` (retry delays). No test seam added to the scheduler — public API (`start`, `stop`, `reload`) is sufficient.
-
-**No scheduler modifications required**: The scheduler's `tick()` method is private but driven entirely through `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync()`. The fake timer runtime processes nested async timers (retry `setTimeout` chains) within a single `advanceTimersByTimeAsync` call.
-
-**CTX_ROOT isolation**: Both `crons.ts` and `cron-execution-log.ts` read `process.env.CTX_ROOT` at call time (not import time), so per-test temp dirs work without module resets for disk paths. `vi.resetModules()` is still called to prevent any module-level state accumulation across tests.

-
-Phase 1 (Subtasks 1.1-1.5) is validated and ready for production use. All critical failure modes (crashes, corruption, retry exhaustion, concurrent fires) have been tested and handled correctly by the implementation.

-  does not delete or overwrite the file (confirmed: cron count unchanged)

-  gamma's absence — fire counts grew from t=12h to t=24h for all crons
-- Gamma resumed firing after restart (fresh `new CronScheduler(...)` + `start()`)

-**Catch-up semantics (key finding)**:
-The CronScheduler fires AT MOST ONE catch-up fire on restart. When gamma's 1h `monitor` cron
-was stopped for 12h and restarted, the scheduler computed `nextFireAt = last_fired_at + 1h`
-(which was in the past), set `nextFireAt = now` (immediate single catch-up), then recomputed
-the next future slot. Growth from t=24h to t=36h was 12-13 fires — matching normal 12h operation

 # CHANGELOG
 
-## [Unreleased] — External Persistent Crons (feat/external-persistent-crons)
+## [0.2.0] — 2026-05-04 — External Persistent Crons
+
+Crons move from session-local (`/loop`, `CronCreate`) to daemon-managed `crons.json` files under `${CTX_ROOT}/state/{agent}/`. Auto-migrates from existing `config.json` on first daemon boot. Fully backward-compatible additive feature.
+
+### Phase 5.4 — Race Hardening & Workspace Teaching
+
+- **iter 9 fix**: `lastGoodSchedule` fallback now distinguishes a legitimately-empty `crons.json` from a corrupt parse failure, so emptying a file no longer keeps stale crons firing.
+- **iter 10 fix**: persist `last_fire_attempted_at` to prevent crash-mid-fire double-fire on next daemon restart.
+- **iter 11 fix**: defer scheduler reload while a fire is in flight, and lazy-create the scheduler when a reload hits a start-window gap (no missed first fire after re-enable).
+- **iter 12 fix**: serialize bus `add-cron` / `update-cron` / `remove-cron` operations to fix lost-update race when concurrent edits land on the same agent.
+- **Race test pins**: dedicated regression tests for iter 9 / 10 / 12 race conditions plus remove-cron mid-fire (no double-fire).
+- **`bus upgrade-cron-teaching` CLI scanner**: scans CLAUDE/AGENTS/ONBOARDING/SKILL files for stale `CronCreate` / `/loop` references and reports advisories. Pure advisory by default; `--apply` for safe substitutions.
+- **`migrate-crons` cron-teaching upgrade banner**: daemon emits one advisory line per agent on first migration, drops `.cron-teaching-checked` marker (idempotent).
 
 ### Phase 5.3 — Failure Mode & Recovery
